name: The Tremont House, Lake and Dearborn Streets

built.note: Opened on Saturday, 29 September 1850 (Andreas vol. 2, p. 502).

research_note: THE TREMONT HOUSE, built by T-3688 for the 1871 scene: Ira Couch's third Tremont, 'a magnificent brick structure', five and a half storeys high on 140 feet of Lake Street by 180 feet of Dearborn, opened in September 1850 at a cost of $75,000 (J. M. Van Osdel, architect; Andreas vol. 2, pp. 501-502). Built to Carbutt's stereograph of it from across the corner. It burned in the small hours of 9 October 1871.

position.symbolic_location: South-east corner of Lake and Dearborn Streets.
position.note: Its Lake Street front on the south building line of Lake Street and its Dearborn Street front on the east building line of Dearborn Street, at the corner Carbutt's stereograph shows it on (the card: 'Tremont House, cor. Lake and Dearborn streets'), its long front running south down Dearborn as the stereograph shows it from across the corner. The building lines are the 1871 scene's streets: today's centrelines, off which each street's carriageway half-width and walk are measured. IT LAPS THE 1835 PLAT'S LAKE STREET BY 2.52 m, AND THAT IS REFUSED IN WRITING, NOT REPAIRED (T-3688; tools/corridor_intrusion_baseline.json `refused`): the corridor is derived from the 1835 street control, and the two tracings disagree by about 2.5 m here; moving the hotel 2.5 m south would set it back from the walk it fronts in its own scene. The footprint's origin is local E 710.99 N -180.78.

derivation.reason: Set on the 1871 plan's street lines (traced from Mitchell's 1870 map) at the corner or frontage the texts name; no platted corner or traced frontage for the 1871 city is in data/traces/street_control.json to recompute it from.

footprint.note: One hundred and forty feet on Lake Street by one hundred and eighty feet on Dearborn (Andreas vol. 2, p. 502).

fire.note: Burned in the small hours of 9 October, when the fire swept north-east from the Court House to the river; it lay in ruins by four o'clock (Andreas vol. 2, p. 739).

blocks.name: the hotel
blocks.note: Five and a half storeys of brick (Andreas: 'a magnificent brick structure ... five and a half stories high'), the half storey an attic of small frieze windows under a bracketed cornice; shops on the ground floor and the hotel's columned entrance on Dearborn Street, as Carbutt's stereograph shows them. Storey heights read through the stereograph's camera.

porches.note: The columned porch over the Dearborn Street entrance, with a balcony on it, as the stereograph shows it.

towers.name: the belvedere
towers.note: The octagonal belvedere on the roof with its railed gallery and little dome, as the stereograph shows it.

value.note: Plan size and storeys from Andreas (vol. 2, p. 502); the fronts read off Carbutt's stereograph (Library of Congress, stereo 1s47905).

composition.note: Plan size and storeys from Andreas; the fronts, the porch and the belvedere from the stereograph; heights read off it.

wall_material.note: 'A magnificent brick structure' (Andreas vol. 2, p. 502); its colour read off the stereograph as a dark common brick.

phases.change_note: Built T-3688 (2026-11-21): the Tremont House stands in the 1871 scene on the landmark_1871 archetype.
